clue.text: Nurse gets right in the fashion

indicators.note: gets right in says the abbreviation for right is placed within the word for nursing

parts.note: to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A nurse who has got the latest style exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets ... in' puts R inside TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is the current direction of style, what is in vogue.

clue.text: A pair of leaders is proverbially better than one

explanation.surface: The saying that two leaders beat one.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'two heads are better than one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads are leaders, so a pair of them; and the proverb holds that a couple of minds beat a single one.

clue.text: At the end of the day it's the object of egalitarians

definitions.text: At the end of the day

explanation.surface: What egalitarians ultimately aim for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of the day' looks like the idiom for 'ultimately', but it literally means dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk comes at day's close; and levelling inequality out is what egalitarians pursue.

clue.text: Make a run for it!

parts.note: the command to bolt could be one word for a sprint, also an old mild oath said in exasperation

explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a quick sprint, and the word is also an exclamation of annoyance.

clue.text: Could be a Manxman admitting to character assassination

explanation.surface: A man from the Isle of Man confessing he has smeared someone's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as I SLANDER, a confession of defamation. The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea; a Manxman lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman lives on an island, so he is an island dweller; and saying 'I slander' is owning up to defaming someone.

clue.text: Come, dear, a ring's in order for this wedding too

indicators.note: in order means the letters are put into their proper arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone proposing again with a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges COME, DEAR, A and RINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding that is another one after a first is a remarriage.

clue.text: Everyone has a yen to make a firm friend

parts.note: all means everyone
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Everyone keen to make a business friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' and 'yen' suggest business and longing, but yen is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a staunch supporter or partner.

clue.text: Old peer is moved to express intense disapproval

indicators.note: is moved says the letters of old peer shift into a new order

explanation.surface: An aged lord is stirred to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore is to lament or condemn strongly.

clue.text: Gives cheering support to radicals

explanation.surface: Someone cheering on political extremists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radicals' looks political but means mathematical roots, as in square roots; the first sense is from 'roots for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporting a team noisily is rooting for it; and radical signs in maths mark square and other roots.

clue.text: The high regard which the fit patient doubtless feels for his doctor

definitions.text: which the fit patient doubtless feels for his doctor

explanation.surface: A healthy patient's esteem for the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means sensible caution or esteem; literally it is the respect of someone who is well.
explanation.definitionFit: It means deep and wary esteem, and literally the regard felt by someone in good health.

clue.text: Manage to discover what a bishop's position is

explanation.surface: Someone managing to find out where a bishop stands.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's see is his diocese, and a bishop is over it: OVER SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage is to supervise; and a bishop sits in charge above his diocese.

clue.text: The song was one Odysseus at first found charming

definitions.text: one Odysseus at first found charming

explanation.surface: A song that charmed the Greek hero when he first heard it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey the nymph of that name kept Odysseus on her island for seven years; it is also a Caribbean song style.
explanation.definitionFit: A West Indian ballad style shares its name with the sea nymph who held Odysseus captive.

clue.text: In this verse pictures of the heroes can be found

definitions.text: In this verse pictures of the heroes can be found

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit inside the words verse pictures, running across their join

explanation.surface: A long poem in which portraits of heroes appear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across versE PICtures; the whole clue also describes such a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroic narrative poem portrays the deeds of legendary warriors.

clue.text: Highland dance which might well appeal to the indulgent pleasure-seeker

definitions.text: might well appeal to the indulgent pleasure-seeker

explanation.surface: A Scottish dance that suits a hedonist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland ___ is a vigorous Scottish solo dance; the word also means a short spell of self-indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a Scottish reel-type dance and also a spree or brief affair.

clue.text: The intelligence which may mean the end of you and me

parts.note: saying no more of something means its end, as in no us
us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: Secret intelligence that could spell doom for both of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No us' would mean we were finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is common sense or practical wit, a synonym for brains.

clue.text: It may indicate a cold scorn

explanation.surface: A gesture that shows chilly contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cold scorn' reads as one phrase, but it splits into a symptom of a cold and contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A runny nose makes you draw air in noisily, and the same nasal sound shows disdain.

clue.text: In the United States English is employed

parts.note: taken as written
US is the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: English being the language used in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being utilised is currently working, occupied.

clue.text: O, Ann, might greed abnormally selfish produce such an attitude?

indicators.note: abnormally says the letters of the preceding words are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Asking whether Ann's greed might make her selfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abnormally' rearranges O, ANN, MIGHT and GREED. In the fable a dog lies in hay it cannot eat, keeping it from the hungry ox.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a spiteful attitude of keeping from others what you cannot use yourself.

clue.text: Have confidence about American currency of late

indicators.note: about means the word for trust goes round the American coin

parts.note: to rely is to have confidence
a cent is a US coin

explanation.surface: Trusting the US dollar in recent times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the trust word round the coin; 'Have confidence' is a verb phrase, matching the verb rely.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, in the near past.

clue.text: Aesthetic creed of the dedicated but penniless painter?

definitions.text: of the dedicated but penniless painter?

explanation.surface: The principle of an artist devoted to work that earns nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a penniless painter makes art just for the sake of making it.
explanation.definitionFit: The slogan holds that painting needs no moral or practical purpose; and a painter unpaid works purely from devotion.

clue.text: Bitter regret suffered by sappers receiving a coded signal

indicators.note: receiving means the sappers take on the coded message after them

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, are the army's sappers
Morse code sends signals as dots and dashes

explanation.surface: Army engineers sorry after receiving a coded message.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in Britain the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep guilt and contrition over a wrong done.

clue.text: Incidentally, a supporter gets so upset

parts.note: a prop is something that supports

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word so on its head, reading it bottom to top

explanation.surface: A fan who gets upset in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SO into OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means by the way, in connection with something mentioned.

clue.text: The French politician is a leading light

parts.note: la is the feminine form of the in French
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A French politician who is a star of public life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a leading light' sounds like an eminent person, but here it is a literal light.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a source of illumination that guides the way.

clue.text: Go off for a holiday

explanation.surface: Going away on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart; and time off work granted, as in annual leave.

clue.text: A prison in a state of agitation

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A jail in turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astir means up and moving, stirred into activity.

clue.text: At liberty now that no charge is being made

definitions.text: now that no charge is being made

explanation.surface: Someone released now that no charges are pressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a criminal charge, but the second sense is a price.
explanation.definitionFit: It means unconfined, and also costing nothing.

clue.text: Just a swings and roundabouts situation

explanation.surface: An even-handed trade-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swings and roundabouts' is the British idiom for gains balancing losses, but here it is literal fairground rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable conduct is just; and a funfair has swings and roundabouts.

clue.text: He hopes to make a quick buck!

definitions.text: He hopes to make a quick buck!

parts.words: He hopes to make a quick buck!
parts.note: a share speculator buying new issues to sell at once for profit, and also a male deer, a buck

explanation.definitionFit: On the stock market the term is a speculator flipping new shares; and a buck is a male deer.

clue.text: What the plane passenger must pay for dry food

definitions.text: What the plane passenger must pay

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it
fare is food, as in simple fare

explanation.surface: An air traveller paying for dried in-flight food.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket price for a flight is what the traveller is charged.

clue.text: Start taking marijuana and tread the road to ruin

explanation.surface: Drug use as the path to downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot is slang for cannabis; the idiom means to deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, begin on cannabis; idiomatically, decline into a ruined state.

clue.text: Strongly denounce vote in the EEC with relative speed

indicators.note: in tells us the voting mark is placed inside the community's initials

parts.note: taken as written
X is the mark made on a ballot paper
a rate is a speed measured relative to time

explanation.surface: Fiercely condemning a vote in the old European Economic Community taken in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts X inside EEC to give EXEC.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or detest loudly, to condemn fiercely.

clue.text: Blustering fellow takes in man of outstanding virtue

indicators.note: takes in means the word for fellow holds another piece within it

parts.note: a guy is a fellow
a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A loud blustering man who welcomes a paragon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' wraps the fellow round the saint; 'Blustering' here describes wind, not a braggart.
explanation.definitionFit: Blustering weather is windy, coming in sudden blasts.
